Document similarity (cosine similarity of TF-IDF vectors)

Source: R/similarity.R
doc_similarity.Rd

Measures how alike the abstracts in a data frame are. Each abstract is turned into a vector of word weights (TF-IDF: a word counts for more when it is frequent in that abstract and rare across the collection), and two abstracts are compared by the cosine of the angle between their vectors: 0 means no words in common, 1 means the same word profile. Text is cleaned the same way as in [topic_model()].

Usage

doc_similarity(
  data,
  text = "abstract",
  id = "bibkey",
  min_doc_freq = 2,
  max_doc_prop = 1,
  min_word_length = 3,
  stopwords = NULL,
  singularize = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per reference.

text

Name of the column holding the text to analyse.

id

Name of a column that identifies each reference (default `"bibkey"`). If it does not exist, row numbers are used.

min_doc_freq

Drop words that occur in fewer than this many abstracts. The default of 2 ignores words that cannot link two abstracts.

max_doc_prop

Drop words that occur in more than this share of the abstracts (1 keeps everything; try 0.5 to remove words common to nearly every abstract).

min_word_length

Drop words shorter than this many letters.

stopwords

Extra words to drop, in addition to [citelens_stopwords()].

singularize

Merge simple plurals (default `TRUE`).

Value

An object of class `citelens_similarity`. Use [similar_to()], [find_duplicates()] and [plot_similarity()] to explore it; the matrix itself is in `$sim`.

Details

Similarity reflects shared vocabulary, not meaning, so two abstracts that use different words for the same idea can look less alike than they are. The result stores a full abstract-by-abstract matrix, which is fine for thousands of abstracts but grows with the square of their number.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens")
refs <- bib_to_df(f)
s <- doc_similarity(refs)
similar_to(s, "syn01", n = 3)
#>   rank    id similarity
#> 1    1 syn05  0.6022649
#> 2    2 syn08  0.5754191
#> 3    3 syn02  0.5753822
